Lessons.Title: Power Functions and Polynomial Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goals: identify power functions and their end behavior; identify polynomials; find polynomial degree and leading coefficient.
A power function is a single term a·x^n. Polynomial functions are finite sums of nonnegative integer powers with real coefficients.
At large |x|, the leading term dominates: even-degree tails have the same sign, odd-degree tails opposite signs. For positive leading coefficients, the right tail rises; negative falls.
Factors reveal real zeros. At a zero of odd multiplicity the curve crosses the horizontal axis; at even multiplicity it touches or bounces.
A degree-n polynomial has at most n distinct real zeros and at most n−1 turning points, and a polynomial graph is continuous and smooth.
Independent Edulytics cool-down: (a) Is 4x³−2x a single power function? (b) Determine tails for −2x⁷+5x². (c) Find degree and real zeros of 3x(x−1)²(x+2).
Independent Try It 1 — Classify polynomial and power. Is 2x²·4x³ a power function? Is x⁵−x a power function?
Independent Try It 2 — Even negative power tails. State end behavior of −5x⁴.
Independent Try It 3 — Leading coefficient after rearranging. For 4x²−x⁶+2x−6 determine degree and leading coefficient.
Independent Try It 4 — Least degree from turning points. A smooth continuous curve changes direction 3 times and tails both rise. What minimum polynomial degree is possible?
Independent Try It 5 — Expand factors and infer tails. Find leading term and degree of 0.2(x−2)(x+1)(x−5).
Independent Try It 6 — Find polynomial zeros. Find intercepts of f(x)=2x³−6x²−20x.
Independent Try It 7 — Maximum turning point count. For degree12 polynomial, state max x-intercepts and turning points.
Independent Try It 8 — Use graph root multiplicity. A polynomial graph touches at x=2 and crosses at x=−1. Find a simple polynomial model.
Independent Try It 9 — Crossing behavior from factors. For f(x)=0.2(x−2)(x+1)(x−5), state intercept crossing behavior.

WorkedExamples.Title: Recognize a single power term
WorkedExamples.Question: For each f(x)=3x⁴, g(x)=x³−x and h(x)=7 identify a power function or sum of powers.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use polynomial definitions, factorization, parity, degree and end behavior.
Steps: f is power a·xⁿ, g is polynomial not single power, h=7·x⁰ is constant power.
WorkedExamples.Answer: f is power a·xⁿ, g is polynomial not single power, h=7·x⁰ is constant power.
WorkedExamples.Check: Verify leading term and evaluate given roots.

WorkedExamples.Title: Even positive end behavior
WorkedExamples.Question: Describe end behavior of f(x)=4x⁶.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use polynomial definitions, factorization, parity, degree and end behavior.
Steps: As x→±∞, f(x)→+∞, positive even leading power.
WorkedExamples.Answer: As x→±∞, f(x)→+∞, positive even leading power.
WorkedExamples.Check: Verify leading term and evaluate given roots.

WorkedExamples.Title: Odd negative end behavior
WorkedExamples.Question: Describe end behavior of f(x)=−2x⁵.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use polynomial definitions, factorization, parity, degree and end behavior.
Steps: As x→−∞ f→+∞ and x→+∞ f→−∞.
WorkedExamples.Answer: As x→−∞ f→+∞ and x→+∞ f→−∞.
WorkedExamples.Check: Verify leading term and evaluate given roots.

WorkedExamples.Method: Use polynomial definitions, factorization, parity, degree and end behavior.

WorkedExamples.Question: A polynomial has three distinct x-intercepts and two changes of direction, crossing the axis each time. What minimum degree is possible?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use polynomial definitions, factorization, parity, degree and end behavior.
Steps: Degree3 is possible; at least3 from distinct zeros, at least3 from two turning points.

KeyConcepts.Title: Power function
KeyConcepts.Definition: One term a·xⁿ with constant a and exponent n≥0 for polynomial power functions.
KeyConcepts.Rule: The exponent is power, a its coefficient.

KeyConcepts.Title: Polynomial definition
KeyConcepts.Definition: Finite sum of nonnegative integer powers of x with real coefficients.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Fractional or negative x powers are not polynomials.

KeyConcepts.Title: Degree
KeyConcepts.Rule: Product degrees add unless zero polynomial factors.

KeyConcepts.Title: Leading coefficient
KeyConcepts.Rule: Leading term determines both end behaviors.

KeyConcepts.Title: Even-degree behavior
KeyConcepts.Definition: Both tails of a polynomial travel in the same vertical direction.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Sign of leading coefficient decides up or down.

KeyConcepts.Title: Odd-degree behavior
KeyConcepts.Definition: Polynomial tails travel in opposite vertical directions.

KeyConcepts.Title: Roots and intercepts
KeyConcepts.Definition: An x-intercept has p(x)=0; y-intercept p(0).

KeyConcepts.Title: Multiplicity
KeyConcepts.Definition: Odd root multiplicity crosses x-axis, even multiplicity touches/bounces.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Graph behavior near a root depends on multiplicity parity.

KeyConcepts.Title: Turning point bound
KeyConcepts.Definition: Degree n≥1 polynomial has at most n−1 turning points.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Number of distinct real roots at most n.

KeyConcepts.Title: Continuity/smoothness
KeyConcepts.Definition: Polynomial graphs are continuous and smooth without corners or discontinuities.
KeyConcepts.Rule: A graph with a hole or jump cannot be a polynomial graph.

Visuals.Title: Polynomial tails from leading term
Visuals.Description: First-party summary of degree parity and leading sign.

SummaryPoints: Power function is one term; polynomial finite sum.
Degree is highest nonzero power and leading coefficient controls tails.
Odd/even degree determines whether tails match.
Degree n bounds real zeros and turning points.

CommonMistakes.Correction: Polynomial powers must be nonnegative integers.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Concluding root multiplicity from leading sign.
Claiming degree n guarantees n real zeros.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: n is only the maximum; some roots can be complex or repeated.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use at most n distinct real zeros.
